t: The Longshan culture is named after the town of Longshan in Shandong, near the Chengziya site found in 1928, and is best known for thin, polished black pottery made on the potter’s wheel.
In the 3rd millennium BCE its population grew sharply: towns were walled with rammed earth, a few centres grew to over 200 hectares, and the dagger-axe points to more frequent warfare.
Around 2000 BCE its population fell sharply and large settlements were abandoned, except in central Henan, where the culture developed into the Bronze Age Erlitou culture.
dyk: Some Longshan men from Shandong stood between 180 and 190 cm tall, taller than any other Neolithic population in the world; the tallest yet found, from Shaanxi, was a youth of about 16–18 who measured 193 cm.
ev: The Miaodigou II phase in Henan, Shanxi and Shaanxi marks the passage from the Yangshao culture to the Henan Longshan
Sheep and goats, domesticated on the Loess Plateau, reach western Henan and then spread across the middle and lower Yellow River
In the late period regional variants flourish, settlements form hierarchies and some thirty towns are walled with rammed earth
The population falls sharply and large centres are abandoned, possibly through climate change at the end of the Holocene Climatic Optimum
The Chengziya site near Longshan in Shandong is found, and excavated in 1930 and 1931
Excavations at Shanxian in western Henan identify the Miaodigou II phase
Kwang-chih Chang describes a uniform “Longshanoid horizon”, which he replaces in 1986 with a “Chinese interaction sphere” of regional cultures

f.homeland: The middle and lower Yellow River valley of northern China: Shandong (Chengziya, near the town of Longshan in Zhangqiu; Liangchengzhen and Yaowangcheng on the Rizhao coast), Henan, southern Hebei, southern Shanxi (Taosi in the Fen River valley) and the Wei River valley in Shaanxi.
f.period: c. 3000–1900 BCE: an early Miaodigou II phase (3000–2600 BCE) in Henan, Shanxi and Shaanxi, then a late period (2600–2000 BCE) of regional variants, the Shandong or “classic” Longshan, Wangwan III, Hougang II, Taosi, Sanliqiao II and Kexingzhuang II (the Shaanxi Longshan); decline towards the end of the 3rd millennium BCE.
f.known: thin-walled, highly polished black “egg-shell” pottery made on the wheel; rammed-earth town walls; centres of over 200 hectares such as Taosi; divination with heated shoulder blades; the first wells of the Yellow River area; copper tools, rings and bells; jade prestige goods; small-scale silk production
f.sources: The Chengziya site, found in 1928 and excavated in 1930 and 1931; excavations at Shanxian in western Henan in the 1950s; regional surveys of settlement hierarchies; plant and animal remains and skeletons; syntheses by Kwang-chih Chang (1963, 1986), Yan Wenming and others.
